GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
status signal; the REST `line` field lied.

Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`

`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).

The local translation is:

| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
|---|---|---|
| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |

`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.

The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
survives as a lint in all three scripts.

`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
session used one anyway.

The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).

## 11. Operating it

    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch

Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
neither publishes a review.

Artefacts:

| Path | Committed | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |

Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
agreeing is intentional redundancy.

Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
not a verdict.

## 12. Deliberately not ported

Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".

* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
  One reviewer session; the cascade
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
  comes from a branch of this single repository.
* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
  allow-list only approximated.
* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).


## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)

A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:

1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   `moot: <reason>`);
2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.

Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.

## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)

The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}

   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}
   384	
   385	CL functions used in the paper are frequently defined over a ``large'' field
   386	$\F_{2^t}$ (e.g., the CL functions used in the low degree tests of
   387	Section~\ref{sec:ldt}).
   388	However, the introspection protocol in Section~\ref{sec:introspection} handles
   389	CL functions defined over $\F_2$.
   390	The following definition and lemma show that CL functions over prime power
   391	fields can be viewed as CL functions over the prime field via a ``downsizing''
   392	operation.
   393	
   394	\begin{definition}[Downsizing CL functions]
   395	  \label{def:cl-downsize}
   396	  Let $V = \F_{q}^n$ be a linear space for a prime power $q=p^t$ for odd $t$.
   397	  Let $L: V \to V$ be a function.
   398	  Let $\downsize(\cdot)$ denote the downsize map from
   399	  Section~\ref{sec:finite-fields} corresponding to the basis
   400	  $\{e_1,\ldots,e_t\}$ of $\F_q$ over $\F_p$ specified by
   401	  Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_basis}.
   402	  In particular, $\downsize$ is linear over $\F_p$, and by
   403	  Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_subspace}, the set $\downsize(V)$ is the linear space
   404	  $\F_p^{nt}$.

1	\section{Types}
     2	\label{sec:types}
     3	
     4	We augment the definition of conditionally linear functions with a construct
     5	we call \emph{types}.
     6	A type~$\tvar$ is an element of a \emph{type set} $\type$, and a $\type$-typed
     7	family of conditionally linear functions is a collection
     8	$\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar\in\type}$ containing a CL function $L_\tvar$ for each
     9	type~$\tvar\in\type$.
    10	The utility of this definition is that it allows us to define another object,
    11	namely conditionally linear distributions parameterized by an undirected graph
    12	$G = (\type, E)$ on the set of types known as a \emph{type graph}.
    13	Given two $\type$-typed families of conditionally linear functions
    14	$\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type}, \{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$, the $(\type,
    15	G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution corresponding to them is the
    16	distribution which samples a pair of types $(\lvar, \rvar)$ uniformly at random
    17	from the edges of~$G$ (with each endpoint having equal probability as being
    18	chosen for $\lvar$ or $\rvar$, respectively) and then samples $(x, y)$ from
    19	$\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    20	The output is the pair $( (\lvar, x), (\rvar, y) )$.
    21	
    22	The normal form verifiers we present in the paper frequently use typed CL
    23	distributions to sample their questions, rather than untyped CL distributions.
    24	Types allow us to model the parts of their question distributions which are
    25	unstructured and unsuitable for being sampled from CL distributions.
    26	A common use of types is to allow the verifier to use previously defined games
    27	as subroutines.
    28	Here, the type helps indicate which subroutine the verifier selects, and an edge
    29	in the type graph between two different types allows us to introduce a test that
    30	cross-checks the results of one subroutine with the results of another.
    31	
    32	Finally, we show how to convert any typed CL distribution into an equivalent (in
    33	the precise sense defined below) untyped CL distribution with two additional
    34	levels, a technique we call \emph{detyping}.
    35	This entails showing how to ``simulate'' the \emph{graph distribution} of $G =
    36	(\type, E)$, i.e.\ the uniform distribution on its edges, using an untyped CL
    37	distribution.
    38	The simulation we give is based on rejection sampling and is only approximate:
    39	its quality degrades exponentially with the number of types in~$\type$.
    40	As a result, we will ensure throughout the paper that all type sets we consider
    41	are of a small, in fact generally constant, size.
    42	
    43	This section is organized as follows.
    44	In \cref{sec:typed-samplers} we define typed variants of CL distributions,
    45	samplers, deciders, and verifiers.
    46	In \cref{sec:graph-dist} we define a CL distribution which samples from the
    47	graph distribution of a given graph $G = (\type, E)$.
    48	In \cref{sec:detype} we define a canonical way to detype typed samplers,
    49	deciders, and verifiers using the graph sampler from \cref{sec:graph-dist}.
    50	We then prove the main result of the section, \cref{lem:detyping-verifiers},
    51	which relates the value of the detyped normal form verifier to the value of
    52	the original typed verifier.

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}

    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}

   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.

   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

   207	/-- Prefix-indexed decomposition data from `lem:cl-kth`. Factor spaces are
   208	represented by their coordinate sets, matching the register-subspace encoding
   209	used by `IsCondLinearOn`. Blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1218-1238`, paper
   210	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   211	structure CLData (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   212	    (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
   213	  /-- The marginal `L_{≤k}`. -/
   214	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
   215	  /-- The factor register selected by a prefix value. -/
   216	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
   217	  /-- The linear map selected by a prefix value. -/
   218	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   219	  /-- Each marginal has the corresponding conditionally linear level. -/
   220	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ (k.val + 1) (marginal k)
   221	  /-- The selected factor registers are pairwise disjoint. -/
   222	  factor_disjoint : ∀ x i j, i ≠ j →
   223	    Disjoint (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) (factor j (clPrefix marginal j x))
   224	  /-- The selected factor registers cover all coordinates. -/
   225	  factor_cover : ∀ x a, ∃ i, a ∈ factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   226	  /-- Each selected linear map is supported on its factor register. -/
   227	  linear_supported : ∀ k u x a, a ∉ factor k u → linear k u x a = 0
   228	  /-- Each marginal is the sum of the preceding selected linear pieces. -/
   229	  sum_formula : ∀ k x, marginal k x =
   230	    ∑ i : Fin ell, if i.val ≤ k.val then
   231	      linear i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   232	        (coordinateRestriction (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) x) else 0
   233	  /-- The final marginal is the original function. -/
   234	  top : ∀ h : 0 < ell,
   235	    marginal ⟨ell - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ = L

   726	  Finset.univ.sup ell

   728	/-- Direct sums over a register partition preserve conditional linearity. The
   729	level-zero case is included explicitly, as required by the local correction to
   730	`lem:cl-func-prod`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1267-1278`, paper
   731	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`. -/
   732	theorem IsCondLinear.directSum {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   733	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
   734	    (V : Fin m → Finset ι) (ell : Fin m → ℕ)
   735	    (L : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   736	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   737	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ i, a ∈ V i)
   738	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (L j)) :
   739	    IsCondLinear (directSumLevel ell) (condLinearDirectSum V L) := by
   740	  classical
   741	  let _sourceIndex : Fin m := ⟨0, hm⟩
   742	  have hLevel (j : Fin m) : ell j ≤ directSumLevel ell :=
   743	    Finset.le_sup (f := ell) (Finset.mem_univ j)
   744	  have hRaised (j : Fin m) :
   745	      IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (directSumLevel ell) (L j) :=
   746	    IsCondLinearOn.mono_level (hL j) (hLevel j)
   747	  have hUnion : Finset.univ.biUnion V = (Finset.univ : Finset ι) := by
   748	    apply Finset.eq_univ_of_forall
   749	    intro a
   750	    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a

   833	  rw [← Fintype.piFinset_update_eq_filter_piFinset_mem u j hs]

   835	  rw [Fintype.prod_eq_mul_prod_subtype_ne _ j]

   837	  rw [hsame]
   838	  apply congrArg (fun n => s.card * n)

   840	  intro i _

   845	/-- The weight of a shared-seed distribution is its fiber cardinality divided

   847	private theorem clDistribution_weight_eq_card_filter_div {K ι : Type*}
   848	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   849	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (z : (ι → K) × (ι → K)) :
   850	    (clDistribution L R).weight z =
   851	      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => (L x, R x) = z).card : Error) /
   852	        Fintype.card (ι → K) := by
   853	  classical
   854	  rw [clDistribution, Distribution.map_weight, uniformDistribution_support]

   858	/-- The CL distribution of coordinate direct sums factors into the component
   859	CL distributions. The equality is stated pointwise on weights, which is the
   860	finite-distribution meaning of the product in `lem:cl-dist-prod`; blueprint
   861	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1285-1290`, paper
   862	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:366-379`. -/
   863	theorem clDistribution_directSum_eq_prod {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   864	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   865	    {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (V : Fin m → Finset ι)
   866	    (ell : Fin m → ℕ)
   867	    (L R : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   868	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   869	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ i, a ∈ V i)
   870	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (L j))
   871	    (hR : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (R j))
   872	    (z : (ι → K) × (ι → K)) :
   873	    (clDistribution (condLinearDirectSum V L) (condLinearDirectSum V R)).weight z =
   874	      ∏ j : Fin m, (clDistribution (L j) (R j)).weight
   875	        (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2) := by
   876	  classical
   877	  let _sourceIndex : Fin m := ⟨0, hm⟩
   878	  let e : (ι → K) ≃ ∀ j, V j → K :=
   879	    coordinatePartitionEquiv V hDisjoint hCover
   880	  let fiber : (j : Fin m) → Finset (V j → K) := fun j =>
   881	    Finset.univ.filter fun x =>
   882	      (L j (extendRegister (V j) x), R j (extendRegister (V j) x)) =
   883	        (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2)
   884	  have hL_support (j : Fin m) (x : ι → K) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) :
   885	      L j x a = 0 :=
   886	    IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem (hL j) x ha
   887	  have hR_support (j : Fin m) (x : ι → K) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) :
   888	      R j x a = 0 :=
   889	    IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem (hR j) x ha
   890	  have hdirect (x : ι → K) :
   891	      (condLinearDirectSum V L x, condLinearDirectSum V R x) = z ↔
   892	        ∀ j,
   893	          (L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x),
   894	              R j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) =
   895	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2) := by
   896	    constructor
   897	    · intro h j
   898	      have hleft : condLinearDirectSum V L x = z.1 := congrArg Prod.fst h
   899	      have hright : condLinearDirectSum V R x = z.2 := congrArg Prod.snd h
   900	      have hleft_parts : ∀ i,
   901	          L i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x) = coordinateRestriction (V i) z.1 := by
   902	        apply (sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover
   903	          (fun i => L i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x))
   904	          (fun i a ha => hL_support i _ a ha) z.1).mp
   905	        exact hleft
   906	      have hright_parts : ∀ i,
   907	          R i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x) = coordinateRestriction (V i) z.2 := by
   908	        apply (sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover
   909	          (fun i => R i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x))
   910	          (fun i a ha => hR_support i _ a ha) z.2).mp

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  A conditionally linear map of level `ell` is a sum of `ell`
     9	linear contributions on pairwise disjoint register subspaces, each contribution
    10	selected by the values of the preceding ones.  The inductive predicate records
    11	this decomposition, and the graph distribution is the law of the type pair.
    12	Equal-level maps over pairwise disjoint coordinate registers have coordinatewise
    13	direct sums whose shared-seed laws factor as products.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`
    18	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`), `def:cl-dist`
    19	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1211-1214`), `lem:cl-concat`
    20	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1247-1261`), and `def:graph-distribution`
    21	(`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1379-1391`).
    22	The paper origins are
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57,282-314`,
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`,
    25	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open scoped BigOperators
    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    33	
    34	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    36	/--
    37	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    38	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    39	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    40	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    41	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    42	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    43	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`,
    44	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    45	-/
    46	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    47	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    48	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    49	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    50	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    51	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    52	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    53	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    54	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    55	
    56	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    57	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    58	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    60	-/
    61	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    62	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    63	
    64	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    65	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    66	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    68	-/
    69	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    70	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    71	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    72	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    73	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    74	      fun x =>
    75	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    76	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    77	
    78	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    79	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    80	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    82	-/
    83	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    84	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    85	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    86	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    87	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    88	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    89	
    90	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    91	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    92	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    93	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    94	-/
    95	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    96	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    97	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    98	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    99	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
   100	
   101	/--
   102	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
   103	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`; paper
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
   105	-/
   106	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   107	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L

   109	/-- The zero conditionally linear function at every level, used to extend the
   110	family `R u` from the image `L(U)` to all indices in the concatenation
   111	construction of `lem:cl-concat`. -/
   112	private def CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   113	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : (ell : ℕ) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   114	  | 0 => .zero
   115	  | ell + 1 => .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => zeroOfLevel ell)
   116	
   117	@[simp]
   118	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   119	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (x : ι → K) :
   120	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) x = 0 := by
   121	  induction ell with
   122	  | zero => rfl
   123	  | succ ell ih =>
   124	      simp [CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval, ih]
   125	
   126	private theorem CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   127	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) :
   128	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   129	      (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) S := by
   130	  induction ell generalizing S with
   131	  | zero => trivial
   132	  | succ ell ih =>
   133	      exact ⟨by simp, fun _ => ih _⟩
   134	
   135	/-- Extending the support set preserves the support invariant. -/
   136	private theorem CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_mono {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   137	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
   138	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S T : Finset ι}
   139	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
   140	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t T := by
   141	  induction t generalizing S T with
   142	  | zero => trivial
   143	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   144	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   145	      refine ⟨hS₁.trans hST, fun y => ih y (hrest y) ?_⟩
   146	      exact Finset.sdiff_subset_sdiff hST (fun _ h => h)

   148	/-- Lift a linear map to the left summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   149	private def condLinearLiftLeft {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   150	    (L : (ιU → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU → K)) :
   151	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where
   152	  toFun x := Sum.elim (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) 0
   153	  map_add' x y := by
   154	    ext i
   155	    cases i with
   156	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   157	    | inr i => simp
   158	  map_smul' c x := by
   159	    ext i
   160	    cases i with
   161	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i
   162	    | inr i => simp
   163	
   164	/-- Lift a linear map to the right summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   165	private def condLinearLiftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   166	    (L : (ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιV → K)) :
   167	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where
   168	  toFun x := Sum.elim 0 (L (fun i => x (.inr i)))
   169	  map_add' x y := by
   170	    ext i
   171	    cases i with
   172	    | inl i => simp
   173	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   174	  map_smul' c x := by
   175	    ext i
   176	    cases i with
   177	    | inl i => simp
   178	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i
   179	
   180	/-- Lift a representation of a conditionally linear function to the right
   181	summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   182	private def CondLinearTerm.liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   183	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] :
   184	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell →
   185	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU ⊕ ιV) ell
   186	  | _, .zero => .zero
   187	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   188	      .succ (S₁.map Function.Embedding.inr) (condLinearLiftRight L₁)
   189	        (by
   190	          intro x i hi
   191	          cases i with
   192	          | inl i => rfl
   193	          | inr i =>
   194	              apply hSupport
   195	              simpa using hi)
   196	        (fun y => liftRight (rest (fun i => y (.inr i))))
   197	
   198	@[simp]
   199	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   200	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   201	    {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell) (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) :
   202	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.liftRight (ιU := ιU) t) x =
   203	      Sum.elim (0 : ιU → K) (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun i => x (.inr i))) := by
   204	  induction t with
   205	  | zero =>
   206	      simp [CondLinearTerm.liftRight, CondLinearTerm.eval]
   207	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   208	      ext i
   209	      cases i <;>
   210	        simp [CondLinearTerm.liftRight, CondLinearTerm.eval, condLinearLiftRight,
   211	          coordinateRestriction, ih]; rfl

   213	private theorem CondLinearTerm.liftRight_supportedOn {K ιU ιV : Type*}
   214	    [Field K] [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   215	    {ell : ℕ} {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell} {S : Finset ιV}
   216	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
   217	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.liftRight (ιU := ιU) t)
   218	      (S.map Function.Embedding.inr) := by
   219	  induction t generalizing S with
   220	  | zero => trivial
   221	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   222	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   223	      refine ⟨Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hS₁, fun y => ?_⟩
   224	      have hsets :
   225	          (S \ S₁).map (Function.Embedding.inr : ιV ↪ ιU ⊕ ιV) =
   226	            S.map Function.Embedding.inr \ S₁.map Function.Embedding.inr := by
   227	        ext i
   228	        cases i <;> simp
   229	      rw [← hsets]
   230	      exact ih (fun i => y (.inr i)) (hrest (fun i => y (.inr i)))

   232	/-- Concatenate a family of conditionally linear representations on the right
   233	register with a conditionally linear representation on the left register, while
   234	recording the prefix accumulated by the preceding left levels. -/
   235	private def CondLinearTerm.concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   236	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   237	    {ell : ℕ} (rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell)
   238	    (acc : ιU → K) :
   239	    {k : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU) k →
   240	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU ⊕ ιV) (ell + k)
   241	  | _, .zero => CondLinearTerm.liftRight (rTerm acc)
   242	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   243	      .succ (S₁.map Function.Embedding.inl) (condLinearLiftLeft L₁)
   244	        (by
   245	          intro x i hi
   246	          cases i with
   247	          | inl i =>
   248	              apply hSupport
   249	              simpa using hi
   250	          | inr i => rfl)
   251	        (fun y => concat rTerm (acc + fun i => y (.inl i))
   252	          (rest (fun i => y (.inl i))))

   254	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   255	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   256	    {ell k : ℕ} (rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell)
   257	    (acc : ιU → K) (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU) k)
   258	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) :
   259	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm acc t) x =
   260	      Sum.elim (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun i => x (.inl i)))
   261	        (CondLinearTerm.eval
   262	          (rTerm (acc + CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun i => x (.inl i))))
   263	          (fun i => x (.inr i))) := by
   264	  induction t generalizing acc with
   265	  | zero =>
   266	      simp [CondLinearTerm.concat, CondLinearTerm.eval]
   267	  | @succ k S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   268	      ext i
   269	      cases i <;>
   270	        simp [CondLinearTerm.concat, CondLinearTerm.eval, condLinearLiftLeft,
   271	          coordinateRestriction, ih, add_assoc] <;> rfl
   272	
   273	private theorem CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   274	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   275	    {ell k : ℕ} {rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell}
   276	    {acc : ιU → K} {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU) k}
   277	    {SU : Finset ιU} {SV : Finset ιV}
   278	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t SU)
   279	    (hr : ∀ u, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) SV) :
   280	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm acc t)
   281	      (SU.map Function.Embedding.inl ∪ SV.map Function.Embedding.inr) := by
   282	  induction t generalizing acc SU with
   283	  | zero =>
   284	      exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_mono
   285	        (CondLinearTerm.liftRight_supportedOn (hr acc)) Finset.subset_union_right
   286	  | @succ k S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   287	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   288	      refine ⟨(Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hS₁).trans Finset.subset_union_left,
   289	        fun y => ?_⟩
   290	      have hrec := ih (fun i => y (.inl i)) (acc := acc + fun i => y (.inl i))
   291	        (hrest (fun i => y (.inl i)))
   292	      have hsets :
   293	          (SU \ S₁).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪ SV.map Function.Embedding.inr =
   294	            (SU.map Function.Embedding.inl ∪ SV.map Function.Embedding.inr) \
   295	              S₁.map Function.Embedding.inl := by
   296	        ext i
   297	        cases i <;> simp
   298	      simpa only [hsets] using hrec

   300	/--
   301	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   302	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   303	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1211-1214`, paper origin
   304	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.

   306	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   307	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   308	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   309	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   310	
   311	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   312	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   313	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   314	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   315	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1247-1261`, paper origin
   316	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   317	-/
   318	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   319	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   320	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   321	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   322	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   323	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   324	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   325	
   326	/--
   327	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   328	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1247-1261`, with
   329	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-292`.
   330	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   331	-/
   332	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   333	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   334	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   335	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   336	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   337	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   338	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   339	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   340	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   341	  classical
   342	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   343	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   344	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   345	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   346	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   347	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   348	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   349	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   350	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   351	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   352	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   353	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   354	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   355	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   356	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   357	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   358	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   359	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   360	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   361	    have huniv :
   362	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   363	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   364	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   365	      ext i
   366	      cases i <;> simp
   367	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   368	  · funext x
   369	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   370	    simp only [zero_add]
   371	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   372	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   373	    rfl
   374	
   375	/--
   376	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   377	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   378	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1379-1391`;
   379	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   380	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   381	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   382	-/
   383	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   384	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   385	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   386	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   387	
   388	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   389	nonempty.  This is not a named statement of the source article; it is
   390	`lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   391	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1393-1403`. -/
   392	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   393	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   394	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   395	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   396	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   397	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   398	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   399	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   400

     8	/-!
     9	# Low-degree polynomial measurements and soundness
    10	
    11	The low-degree question laws have uniform point and coordinate-index marginals,
    12	and every sampled line is incident to its paired point.  Polynomial outcomes
    13	are bounded multivariate polynomials, and the corresponding projective
    14	strategies satisfy the low-degree soundness theorem used in the QPBT argument.
    15	
    16	## References

    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:200-238`. Their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-287,392-480`.
    21	The dimension-divisibility hypothesis is documented in
    22	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    23	-/

    39	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
    40	vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
    41	private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    42	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    43	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    44	  invFun p := fun i =>
    45	    match i with
    46	    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
    47	    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
    48	    | .inr j => p.2 j
    49	  left_inv z := by
    50	    funext i
    51	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
    52	    · rfl
    53	    · cases u
    54	      rfl
    55	    · rfl
    56	  right_inv p := by
    57	    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
    58	    rfl

    64	      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
    65	  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
    66	      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
    67	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
    68	  calc
    69	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
    70	        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
    71	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
    72	          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]

    74	    _ = ((uniformDistribution

    77	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by

   312	noncomputable instance polyFuncFintype (m : ℕ) (K : Type*)
   313	    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) := by
   314	  letI : Finite ↥(polyFunc m K d) := Module.finite_of_finite K

   317	/-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite
   318	coefficient semiring. -/

   320	    [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)

   324	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   325	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=

   331	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   332	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
   333	    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
   334	    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   335	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=

   339	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   340	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d

   343	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   344	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   345	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	The low-degree component of the Pauli basis test has finite question and answer
    10	alphabets.  Its question maps act explicitly on the point, coordinate, and
    11	direction registers of the ambient coefficient space and have recursive
    12	conditionally linear representations of levels one, two, and three.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-192`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	The exact decomposition of a scalar seed into its coordinate index and its
    21	residue records the balance assertion for the map `chi` in the same source
    22	definition.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT

    33	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    34	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    35	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    36	`def:ld-game` in
    37	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, with paper origin
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    39	-/
    40	structure LdParams where
    41	  q : ℕ
    42	  m : ℕ
    43	  d : ℕ
    44	  k : ℕ
    45	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    46	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    47	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    48	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    49	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    50	
    51	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    52	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    53	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    54	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    55	
    56	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    57	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified

    64	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    65	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.

    69	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K

    72	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    73	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    76	  | point

    81	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint

    96	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=

   100	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   111	/-- The zero-based coordinate index corresponding to the paper's map `χ`:
   112	`chiIndex P s` represents `χ(s) - 1` in the fixed field representation.  This
   113	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   114	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   116	-/
   117	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   118	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   119	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   120	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   121	
   122	/-! ### Formalization-only coordinate-index fibers
   123	
   124	The following decomposition supplies the equal-fiber calculation used in the
   125	uniform coordinate-index law.
   126	-/
   127	
   128	/-- The common residue set in a fiber of `chiIndex` is nonempty.  This is part
   129	of the exact seed decomposition supporting the balance assertion in
   130	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `lem:chi-seed-fibers`, paper
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:215-221`.
   132	-/
   133	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   134	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   135	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   136	    rw [hq]
   137	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm
   138	
   139	/-- Divisibility identifies the scalar cardinality with the product of the
   140	coordinate-index cardinality and the common fiber cardinality.  This supports
   141	`lem:chi-seed-fibers` in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   142	theorem LdParams.seedFiberProduct_eq (L : LdParams) :
   143	    L.q = L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   144	  (Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd).symm
   145	
   146	/-- Casting between equal finite cardinalities preserves the underlying
   147	natural-number representative. -/
   148	@[simp] private theorem equivCastFin_val {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (i : Fin m) :
   149	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin h) i).val = i.val := by
   150	  subst n
   151	  rfl
   152	
   153	/-- A scalar seed is uniquely a coordinate index and a residue in its
   154	`chiIndex` fiber.  This is the exact decomposition underlying
   155	`lem:chi-seed-fibers` in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   156	noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   157	    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
   158	  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|
   159	    (Equiv.cast <| congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq).trans
   160	      finProdFinEquiv.symm
   161	
   162	/-- The coordinate component of the exact seed decomposition is `chiIndex`. -/
   163	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
   164	    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
   165	  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩
   166	  have hquot : (binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   167	    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
   168	    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
   169	    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
   170	  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
   171	  apply Fin.ext
   172	  change
   173	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
   174	      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
   175	      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val
   176	  rw [equivCastFin_val]
   177	  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
   178	  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq

   350	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   351	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   352	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   353	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   354	        rfl
   355	  map_smul' c x := by

   359	    · simp

   362	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   363	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   364	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   365	        rfl

   426	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the scalar register

   454	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the point-register projection as a linear
   455	map on the ambient low-degree space. -/
   456	private def ldPointLinear (P : LdParams) :
   457	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   458	  toFun := ldPointCL P
   459	  map_add' x y := by
   460	    funext i
   461	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp [ldPointCL]
   462	  map_smul' c x := by
   463	    funext i
   464	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp [ldPointCL]

   466	/-- The point projection is a one-level conditionally linear function. This is
   467	the level assertion for `L_Point` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   468	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:61-71`, paper
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:203-207`. -/
   470	theorem isCondLinear_ldPointCL (P : LdParams) :
   471	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 1 (ldPointCL P) := by
   472	  refine ⟨.succ Finset.univ (ldPointLinear P)
   473	      (fun _ i hi => absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi) (fun _ => .zero),
   474	    ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ => trivial⟩, ?_⟩
   475	  funext x
   476	  have hx : coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ : Finset (LdIndex P)) x = x := by
   477	    funext i
   478	    simp [coordinateRestriction]
   479	  change ldPointCL P (coordinateRestriction Finset.univ x) + 0 = ldPointCL P x
   480	  rw [hx, add_zero]
