   482	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a two-level representation of the
   483	affine-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   484	private noncomputable def ldALineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   485	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 2 :=
   486	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   487	    fun y =>
   488	      .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   489	        (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y))))
   490	        (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   491	        fun _ => .zero
   492	
   493	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a three-level representation of the
   494	diagonal-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   495	private noncomputable def ldDLineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   496	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 3 :=
   497	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   498	    fun y =>
   499	      .succ (ldDirectionRegister P)
   500	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))
   501	        (ldDirectionCLLinear_supported P _)
   502	        fun w =>
   503	          .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   504	            (ldPointCLLinear P (LdSpace.direction w))
   505	            (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   506	            fun _ => .zero

   508	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is
   509	`lem:ld-aline-level`, the level-2 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   510	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:73-83`, paper
   511	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   512	-/
   513	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   514	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   515	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   516	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   517	  funext x
   518	  have hseed :
   519	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   520	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   521	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   522	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   523	  have hval :
   524	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   525	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   526	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   527	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   528	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   529	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   530	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   531	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   532	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   533	    rw [hseed]
   534	  rw [hval]
   535	  funext i
   536	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   537	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   538	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   539	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   540	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   541	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   542	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   543	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   544	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   545	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   546	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   547	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]
   548	
   549	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is
   550	`lem:ld-dline-level`, the level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   551	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper origin
   552	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   553	-/
   554	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   555	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   556	  refine ⟨ldDLineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   557	    ⟨ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ =>
   558	      ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   559	  funext x
   560	  have hseed :
   561	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   562	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   563	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   564	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   565	  have hdir :
   566	      LdSpace.direction
   567	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   568	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) =
   569	        prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) := by
   570	    funext j
   571	    change prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   572	        (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j = _
   573	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction]
   574	  have hval :
   575	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldDLineTerm P) x =
   576	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   577	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   578	              (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   579	            (ldPointCLLinear P
   580	                (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   581	                (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) := by
   582	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   583	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   584	            (chiIndex P
   585	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   586	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   587	          (ldPointCLLinear P
   588	              (LdSpace.direction
   589	                (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   590	                  (chiIndex P
   591	                    (LdSpace.seed
   592	                      (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   593	                  (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)))
   594	              (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) = _
   595	    rw [hseed, hdir]
   596	  rw [hval]
   597	  funext i
   598	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   599	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) +
   600	        (lineRepMap
   601	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   602	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0)) =
   603	      lineRepMap (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   604	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   605	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, zero_add, add_zero]
   606	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   607	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   608	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero]
   609	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   610	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   611	            (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j +
   612	          ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) =
   613	      prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) j
   614	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction, zero_add, add_zero, add_zero]
   615	
   616	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   617	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
   618	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   619	-/
   620	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   621	
   622	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   623	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   624	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   625	-/
   626	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   627	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   628	  Distribution.map
   629	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   630	    (fun s =>
   631	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

   634	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in

   637	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   639	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   640	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)

     4	/-! # Typed conditionally linear distributions
     5	
     6	Typed question distributions first sample an ordered edge of the type graph and
     7	then sample the corresponding pair of conditionally linear images of one common
     8	uniform seed.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:typed-cl-functions` and `def:typed-cl-distributions` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1370-1418`, with paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-94`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	/-- A typed family whose member at every type is `ell`-level conditionally
    22	linear. This predicate generalizes `def:typed-cl-functions` by permitting an
    23	arbitrary type `T`; concrete source-facing uses supply a finite type. Blueprint
    24	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1370-1374`, paper
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-63`. -/
    26	def IsTypedCondLinearFamily (K T : Type*) [Field K]
    27	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    28	    (ell : ℕ) (L : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    29	  ∀ t, IsCondLinear ell (L t)
    30	
    31	/-- The typed CL distribution: sample a type pair from the graph distribution,
    32	then bind it to the CL distribution selected by those two types. This is
    33	`def:typed-cl-distributions`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1414-1418`, paper
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    35	noncomputable def typedCLDistribution {K T ι : Type*}
    36	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    37	    [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    38	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty)
    39	    (L R : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
    40	    Distribution ((T × (ι → K)) × (T × (ι → K))) :=
    41	  Distribution.bind (graphDistribution E hE) fun uv =>
    42	    (clDistribution (L uv.1) (R uv.2)).map fun xy =>
    43	      ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))
    44	
    45	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

270	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   271	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   272	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   273	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   274	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   275	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   276	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   277	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}
   278	
   279	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   280	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   281	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   282	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P)
   283	
   284	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the direction
   285	coordinates of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   286	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   287	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P)
   288	
   289	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   290	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   291	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   292	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   293	  toFun x := fun i =>
   294	    match i with
   295	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   296	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   297	    | .inr _ => 0
   298	  map_add' x y := by
   299	    funext i
   300	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   301	  map_smul' c x := by
   302	    funext i
   303	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   304	
   305	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   306	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   307	other coordinate. -/
   308	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   309	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   310	  toFun x := fun i =>
   311	    match i with
   312	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   313	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   314	    | .inr _ => 0
   315	  map_add' x y := by
   316	    funext i
   317	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   318	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   319	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   320	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   321	      rfl
   322	    · simp
   323	    · simp
   324	  map_smul' c x := by
   325	    funext i
   326	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   327	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   328	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   329	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   330	      rfl
   331	    · simp
   332	    · simp
   333	
   334	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   335	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   336	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   337	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   338	  toFun x := fun k =>
   339	    match k with
   340	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   341	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   342	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   343	  map_add' x y := by
   344	    funext k
   345	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   346	    · simp
   347	    · simp
   348	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   349	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   350	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   351	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   352	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   353	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   354	        rfl
   355	  map_smul' c x := by
   356	    funext k
   357	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   358	    · simp
   359	    · simp
   360	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   361	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   362	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   363	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   364	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   365	        rfl

   367	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the shared-scalar map vanishes
   368	outside the scalar register. -/
   369	private theorem ldSeedLinear_supported (P : LdParams) :
   370	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldSeedRegister P →
   371	      ldSeedLinear P x i = 0 := by
   372	  intro x i hi
   373	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   374	  · rfl
   375	  · cases u
   376	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_singleton_self _) hi
   377	  · rfl
   378	
   379	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the canonical-representative map
   380	vanishes outside the point register. -/
   381	private theorem ldPointCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   382	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldPointRegister P →
   383	      ldPointCLLinear P v x i = 0 := by
   384	  intro x i hi
   385	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   386	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hi
   387	  · rfl
   388	  · rfl
   389	
   390	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the prefix-zeroing map vanishes
   391	outside the direction register. -/
   392	private theorem ldDirectionCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   393	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (k : LdIndex P), k ∉ ldDirectionRegister P →
   394	      ldDirectionCLLinear P i x k = 0 := by
   395	  intro x k hk
   396	  rcases k with (j | u) | j
   397	  · rfl
   398	  · rfl
   399	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hk

   401	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point register is disjoint from
   402	the scalar register. -/
   403	private theorem ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams) :
   404	    ldPointRegister P ⊆ Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P := by
   405	  intro i hi
   406	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi

   409	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the direction register is disjoint
   410	from the scalar register. -/
   411	private theorem ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams) :
   412	    ldDirectionRegister P ⊆ Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P := by
   413	  intro i hi
   414	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   415	  simp [ldSeedRegister]

   417	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point register is disjoint from
   418	both the scalar and the direction registers. -/
   419	private theorem ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction (P : LdParams) :
   420	    ldPointRegister P ⊆
   421	      (Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P) \ ldDirectionRegister P := by

   423	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   424	  simp [ldSeedRegister, ldDirectionRegister]

   426	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the scalar register
   427	leaves the shared scalar coordinate unchanged. -/
   428	private theorem coordinateRestriction_seed (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   429	    coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) =
   430	      x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) := by
   431	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldSeedRegister P :=
   432	    Finset.mem_singleton_self _
   433	  simp [coordinateRestriction, hmem]

   435	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the point register
   436	leaves the point block unchanged. -/
   437	private theorem coordinateRestriction_point (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   438	    LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) = LdSpace.point x := by
   439	  funext j
   440	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldPointRegister P :=

   444	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the direction register

   446	private theorem coordinateRestriction_direction (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   447	    LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) =
   448	      LdSpace.direction x := by
   449	  funext j

   454	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the point-register projection as a linear
   455	map on the ambient low-degree space. -/
   456	private def ldPointLinear (P : LdParams) :
   457	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   458	  toFun := ldPointCL P
   459	  map_add' x y := by
   460	    funext i
   461	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp [ldPointCL]
   462	  map_smul' c x := by
   463	    funext i
   464	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp [ldPointCL]

   466	/-- The point projection is a one-level conditionally linear function. This is

   470	theorem isCondLinear_ldPointCL (P : LdParams) :
   471	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 1 (ldPointCL P) := by
   472	  refine ⟨.succ Finset.univ (ldPointLinear P)
   473	      (fun _ i hi => absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi) (fun _ => .zero),
   474	    ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ => trivial⟩, ?_⟩
   475	  funext x
   476	  have hx : coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ : Finset (LdIndex P)) x = x := by
   477	    funext i
   478	    simp [coordinateRestriction]
   479	  change ldPointCL P (coordinateRestriction Finset.univ x) + 0 = ldPointCL P x
   480	  rw [hx, add_zero]

   482	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a two-level representation of the
   483	affine-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   484	private noncomputable def ldALineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   485	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 2 :=
   486	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   487	    fun y =>
   488	      .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   489	        (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y))))
   490	        (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   491	        fun _ => .zero
   492	
   493	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a three-level representation of the
   494	diagonal-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   495	private noncomputable def ldDLineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   496	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 3 :=
   497	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   498	    fun y =>
   499	      .succ (ldDirectionRegister P)
   500	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))
   501	        (ldDirectionCLLinear_supported P _)
   502	        fun w =>
   503	          .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   504	            (ldPointCLLinear P (LdSpace.direction w))
   505	            (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   506	            fun _ => .zero
   507	
   508	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is
   509	`lem:ld-aline-level`, the level-2 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   510	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:73-83`, paper
   511	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   512	-/
   513	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   514	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   515	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   516	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   517	  funext x
   518	  have hseed :
   519	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   520	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   521	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   522	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   523	  have hval :
   524	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   525	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   526	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   527	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   528	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   529	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   530	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   531	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   532	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   533	    rw [hseed]
   534	  rw [hval]
   535	  funext i
   536	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   537	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   538	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   539	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   540	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   541	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   542	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   543	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   544	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   545	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   546	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   547	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]
   548	
   549	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is
   550	`lem:ld-dline-level`, the level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   551	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper origin
   552	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   553	-/
   554	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   555	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   556	  refine ⟨ldDLineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   557	    ⟨ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ =>
   558	      ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   559	  funext x
   560	  have hseed :
   561	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   562	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   563	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   564	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   565	  have hdir :
   566	      LdSpace.direction
   567	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   568	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) =

   959	  We say that the tuple $\qldparams=(q, m, d)$ is \emph{admissible} if $q$ is

   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show
   966	that it is a (typed) CL distribution.
   967	The question types in the game $\game^\pauli$ are
   968	\begin{equation}
   969	  \label{eq:pauli-type}
   970	  \type^\pauli= \bigl( \{\Point, \ALine, \DLine, \Pauli, \Pair \} \times \{X,Z\} \bigr)
   971	  \cup \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair\}\;,
   972	\end{equation}
   973	where $\type^\ms$ is the question type set of the Magic Square game defined in
   974	Section~\ref{sec:ms}.

   978	
   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1004	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Variable_j$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,9\}$, then set $x_w
  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}

   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three

   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.

   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.

 /-! # Structure and direct sums of conditionally linear functions
 
 A conditionally linear map admits a prefix decomposition, and conditionally
 linear maps and their shared-seed distributions are stable under finite
 coordinate direct sums.  A representation may be raised to a larger level by
 adjoining zero linear contributions, after which equal-level representations
 combine coordinatewise on pairwise disjoint registers.

     [DecidablePred p] [DecidablePred q] (hpq : ∀ a, p a ↔ q (e a)) :
     (Finset.univ.filter p).card = (Finset.univ.filter q).card := by
   classical
   have hmap : (Finset.univ.filter p).map e.toEmbedding = Finset.univ.filter q := by
     ext b

     ((Finset.univ : Finset (∀ i, B i)).filter fun x => x j ∈ s).card =
       s.card * ∏ i : {i // i ≠ j}, Fintype.card (B i.1) := by
   let u : ∀ i, Finset (B i) := fun _ => Finset.univ
   have hs : s ⊆ u j := Finset.subset_univ s
   rw [← Fintype.piFinset_univ]
   rw [← Fintype.piFinset_update_eq_filter_piFinset_mem u j hs]
   rw [Fintype.card_piFinset]
   rw [Fintype.prod_eq_mul_prod_subtype_ne _ j]
   have hsame : Function.update u j s j = s := by simp
   rw [hsame]
   apply congrArg (fun n => s.card * n)
   apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
   intro i _
   have hne : Function.update u j s i.1 = u i.1 := by simp [i.2]
   rw [hne]
   simp [u]

     · intro h j
       have hleft : condLinearDirectSum V L x = z.1 := congrArg Prod.fst h

         prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) := by
     funext j
     change prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
         (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j = _
     rw [coordinateRestriction_direction]
   have hval :
       CondLinearTerm.eval (ldDLineTerm P) x =
         ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
           (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
               (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
             (ldPointCLLinear P
                 (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
                 (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) := by
     change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
         (ldDirectionCLLinear P
             (chiIndex P
               (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
             (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
           (ldPointCLLinear P
               (LdSpace.direction
                 (ldDirectionCLLinear P
                   (chiIndex P
                     (LdSpace.seed
                       (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
                   (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)))
               (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) = _
     rw [hseed, hdir]
   rw [hval]
   funext i
   rcases i with (j | u) | j
   · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) +
         (lineRepMap
           (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
           (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0)) =
       lineRepMap (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
         (LdSpace.point x) j
     rw [hpoint, zero_add, zero_add, add_zero]
   · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
         ((0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
     rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero]
   · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
         (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
             (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j +
           ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) =
       prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) j
     rw [coordinateRestriction_direction, zero_add, add_zero, add_zero]
 
 /-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
 `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
 -/
 abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
 
 /-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
 `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
 origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
     Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   Distribution.map
     (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
     (fun s =>
       ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
 
 /-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
 answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
 the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`; paper
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`; paper
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
 -/
 inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   deriving DecidableEq
 
 /-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
 instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
     ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
       (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
 
 /-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
 finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
 -/
 noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
     LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   toFun
     | .pointVals a => .inl a
     | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
     | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   invFun
     | .inl a => .pointVals a
     | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
     | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   right_inv := by
     intro x
     cases x with
     | inl a => rfl
     | inr x =>
         cases x with
         | inl a => rfl
         | inr a => rfl
 
 instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
 
 noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
 
 /-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
 representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
-blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
     (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
 
 /-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
 Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
-`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   match t, a with
   | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   | _, _ => false
 
 /-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
-`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
     (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
     (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
     point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
       ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
 
 /-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
-`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
     (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
     (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
     point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
       ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
 
 /-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
 constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:173-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
     LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   open Classical in
   fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
       if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
         match tA, tB, a, b with
         | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
         | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
             decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
         | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
             decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
         | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
             decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
         | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
             decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
         | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
         | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
         | _, _, _, _ => true
       else false
 
 /-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-192`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 -/
 noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   μ_prob := by
     exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
       (uniformDistribution_isProbability ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)) _
   decide := ldWinPredicate P
 
 end
 
 end MIPStarRE.QPBT

 /-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
 vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
 private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
     LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
   toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
   invFun p := fun i =>
     match i with
     | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
     | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
     | .inr j => p.2 j
   left_inv z := by
     funext i
     rcases i with (j | u) | j
     · rfl
     · cases u
       rfl
     · rfl
   right_inv p := by
     obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
     rfl
 
 /-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point block of a uniformly random
 ambient vector is uniform. -/
 private theorem map_uniformDistribution_point (L : LdParams) :
     (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
       uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
   have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
       uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
     uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
   calc
     (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
         = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
             Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
           rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
           rfl
     _ = ((uniformDistribution
           (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
             Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
     _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
           rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]
     _ = uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := uniformDistribution_map_fst

 private theorem map_uniformDistribution_seed (L : LdParams) :
     (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed =
       uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L) := by
   have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
       uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
     uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
   calc
     (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed
         = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
             Prod.fst).map Prod.snd := by
           rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
           rfl
     _ = ((uniformDistribution
           (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
             Prod.fst).map Prod.snd := by rw [hsplit]
     _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.snd := by
           rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]
     _ = uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L) := uniformDistribution_map_snd

     [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)

 noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
     [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι

     [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
     [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι

 def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   let lineEdges :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
       Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
       (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
         Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
       (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
         Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   let basisEdges :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
       Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
       ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
         Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   let pairEdges :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
       Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)

       Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
         Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

     | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
     | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
     | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
     | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
     | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
     | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   invFun
     | .inl a => .value a
     | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
     | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
     | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
     | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
     | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
     | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   left_inv := by
     intro x
     cases x <;> rfl
   right_inv := by
     intro x
     cases x with
     | inl a => rfl
     | inr x =>
         cases x with
         | inl a => rfl
         | inr x =>
             cases x with
             | inl a => rfl
             | inr x =>
                 cases x with
                 | inl a => rfl
                 | inr x =>
                     cases x with
                     | inl a => rfl
                     | inr x =>
                         cases x with
                         | inl a => rfl
                         | inr a => rfl
 
 noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
 
 instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   ⟨.bit 0⟩
 
 /-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
 fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
 self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`; paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
 -/
 noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
     (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
     (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   fixedBinTrace P.model
     (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
 
 /-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
 `eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
-`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
 -/
 noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
     (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
 
 /-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
 well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
-`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   match t, a with
   | .point _, .value _ => true
   | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   | _, _ => false
 
 /-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
     (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
     (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
     pauliPointBlock W point =
         pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
           (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
       evalCoefficient f t = a
 
 /-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
     (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
     (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
     pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
         t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
       evalCoefficient f t = a
 
 /-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
     (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
 
 /-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
-`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
     (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
     (match W with
     | .X => bits.1 = β
     | .Z => bits.2 = β)
 
 /-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
     (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
     fixedBinTrace P.model
       (a * (match W with
       | .X => pauliRXBlock z
       | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
 
 /-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
 The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
 Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`; paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
     (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
     (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
         fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
     (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
         fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
 
 /-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
-`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
+`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:470-506`,
 paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
 -/
 noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
     PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   open Classical in
   fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
     if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
       if tA = tB then
         decide (a = b)
       else
         match tA, tB, a, b with
       | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
       | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
       | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
       | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
       | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
       | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
       | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
           decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
       | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
           decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
       | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
       | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
           if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
       | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
           if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
             decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
               msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
           else true
       | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
           if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
             decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
               msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
           else true
       | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
           decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
       | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
           decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
         | _, _, _, _ => true
     else false
 
 /-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
 `def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:384-506`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
 -/
 noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   μ_prob := by sorry
   decide := pauliWinPredicate P
 
 end
 
 end MIPStarRE.QPBT

 # The Pauli basis test
 
 This file supplies the finite question and answer alphabets, the typed
 conditionally-linear question sampler, and the Boolean win predicate for the
 Pauli basis test.  The quantitative soundness theorem is isolated in
 `Soundness.lean`.
 
 ## References
 
 The source-facing nodes are `def:admissible`, `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
 and `def:pauli-win-predicate` in
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-367`; their paper origin is
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:368-506`; their paper origin is
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-1225`.
 -/
 
 open scoped BigOperators
 
 namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
 
 open MIPStarRE.LDT
 
 noncomputable section
 
 /-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
 uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
 self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
 is `def:admissible` in
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:368-382`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
 -/
 structure AdmissibleParams where
   q : ℕ
   m : ℕ
   d : ℕ
   hd : 1 ≤ d
   hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
   hdvd : m ∣ q
 
 /-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
 the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:368-382`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
 -/
 theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
   sorry
 
 /-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
 compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
-quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
+quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:368-382`; paper
 origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
 -/
 noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
   fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
 
 /-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
 a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
 hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin

 def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
   q := P.q
   m := P.m
   d := P.d
   k := 1
   hm := P.one_le_m
   hd := P.hd
   hk := by decide
   hq := P.hq
   hdvd := P.hdvd

 the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
 `def:admissible`, blueprint
-`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:368-382`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.

 abbrev PauliScalar (P : AdmissibleParams) := P.model.K

-`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:384-428`,

   | point (W : PauliKind)
   | aline (W : PauliKind)
   | dline (W : PauliKind)
   | pauli (W : PauliKind)
   | pairW (W : PauliKind)
   | pair

 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.

   (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)

-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:384-428`; paper origin

 `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-945`.

 `V_X ⊕ V_Z ⊕ V_I ⊕ V_V ⊕ V_{R_X} ⊕ V_{R_Z}` from the blueprint. -/
 /-- The `V_X` block of an ambient Pauli vector (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:384-428`; paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`). -/
 def pauliXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl i)))))
 
 /-- The `V_Z` block of an ambient Pauli vector in `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
-blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:384-428`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
 -/
 def pauliZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=

 def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   let lineEdges :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
       Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪

         Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
       (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
         Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   let basisEdges :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
       Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
       ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
         Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   let pairEdges :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
       Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   let msEdges' :=
     (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
       Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
         Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

     [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) := by

 /-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite
 coefficient semiring. -/
 noncomputable abbrev PolyIndex (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
     [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)
 
 /-- A POVM indexed by one bounded multivariate polynomial. -/
 noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
     [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι
 
 /-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may

-Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:164-171`, paper
+Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:200-207`, paper
 `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
 noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
     [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
     [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
 
 /-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
 noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
 
 /-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
 noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
 
 /-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
 def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
     (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1

    15	\subsection{The classical low-degree test}
    16	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    17	
    18	We begin with a generalization of the classical low-degree test known as the
    19	``simultaneous individual low-degree test''.
    20	We sometimes refer to this as the ``classical low-degree test'' for short.
    21	The low-degree test is used as a subroutine in the Pauli Basis test (see
    22	Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier}) as well as the answer-reduction normal form
    23	verifier (see Section~\ref{sec:ans}).
    24	We describe the test as a nonlocal game in Section~\ref{sec:ld-game} and show
    25	that the question distribution can be implemented as a (typed) conditionally
    26	linear distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL
    27	distributions).

    29	
    30	\subsubsection{The game}
    31	\label{sec:ld-game}
    32	
    33	The game $\game^\ld$ is parametrized by a tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
    34	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
    35	and $m$ divides $q$.
    36	We sometimes write $\game^\ld_\ldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
    37	classical low-degree test on the parameter tuple $\ldparams$.
    38	
    39	We first provide a high-level description of the game for $k=1$.
    40	It is based on the low-individual degree variant of the multilinearity test
    41	of~\cite{babai1991non}, where one player (called the ``points player'') receives
    42	a random point $u \in \F_q^m$, and the other player (called the ``lines
    43	player'') receives a random axis-parallel line $\line$ that contains $u$, i.e.\
    44	the line parallel to the $i$-th axis which goes through point $u$, for uniformly
    45	random $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$.
    46	The points player is supposed to respond with a value $a \in \F_q$, and the
    47	lines player is supposed to respond with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of
    48	degree at most $d$ such that $f_\line(u_i) = a$, where $u_i$ is the $i$-th
    49	coordinate of $u$.
    50	
    51	Suppose the players agree beforehand on a global polynomial $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$
    52	such that every variable has degree at most $d$.
    53	Then a winning strategy is the following: the points player responds with
    54	$g(u)$, and the lines player responds with the univariate polynomial $f_\line$
    55	that is the restriction of $g$ to line $\line$; formally, for $t \in \F_q$,
    56	\[f_\line(t)=g(u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{i-1},t,u_{i+1},\ldots,u_m)\;.\] It is easy to
    57	see that $f_\line(t)$ has degree at most $d$ in the variable $t$.
    58	Thus in this case the players will pass the low-degree test with probability
    59	$1$.
    60	The low-degree testing theorem states that the converse approximately holds: if
    61	the players pass the low-degree test with probability close to $1$, then their
    62	responses must be approximately consistent (in some sense) with a global
    63	polynomial $g$ with individual degree $d$.
    64	
    65	When $k > 1$, the players are supposed to respond with a \emph{tuple} of
    66	answers; and the test is intended to check that the players' responses are

    68	polynomials where every variable has degree at most $d$.

    71	lines-versus-points'' test just described.
    72	In addition, we have two other subtests.

   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

# Formalization Patterns

Key design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the
gap between paper-level mathematics and a compilable Lean proof.

This document is intended for contributors who need to understand *why* the
Lean code is structured as it is, and for reviewers who need to recognize
these patterns when reading PRs.  It complements the individual chapter audits
in `audits/`, the proof-integrity rules in the lean-conventions skill (addenda:
`docs/project_conventions.md`), and the
proof-gap protocol in `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.

## Table of Contents

1. [Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations](#pattern-1-source-faithful-statements-and-internal-proof-obligations)
2. [Blueprint–Lean synchronization](#pattern-2-blueprintlean-synchronization)
3. [Split-module architecture](#pattern-3-split-module-architecture)
4. [Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)
5. [Temporary obligation-structure pattern](#pattern-5-temporary-obligation-structure-pattern)
6. [Paper-gap documentation pattern](#pattern-6-paper-gap-documentation-pattern)
